newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Australian paedophile suspect fights extradition.
newsitem.headline: Australian paedophile suspect fights extradition.

text.p: Lawyer for Australian paedophile suspect Phillip Bell asked a South African court on Tuesday to overturn a ruling ordering Bell's extradition to stand trial back home.
Bell faces 215 sex offences relating to boys aged 10 to 18 in Australia. He is in police custody awaiting a final decision.
His lawyer Allan Frost argued Bell's constitutional rights had been infringed by his detention since he was unable to challenge evidence against him.
State advocate Carl Fischer countered by arguing it was not the responsibility of South African judicial authorities to decide the merits of the charges against Bell.
"This is a matter for the Australian prosecuting authorities and not that of South Africa. It is not our position to formulate what constitutes charges in their law," Fischer said.
The two judges hearing the argument have reserved judgment, without setting a date when their ruling can be expected.
A South African magistrate ruled in February that Bell should be extradited to Australia to stand trial.
Once the high court makes its ruling, his extradition is subject to the final approval of South African Justice Minister Dullah Omar.
Bell, 62, was arrested in the surfing mecca of Jeffrey's Bay -- where he ran a surfing school for youngsters -- in January after a 10-month worldwide police hunt.
